prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules induce proximity between a target protein and the ubiquitin-proteasome system

statement.case_for: Seven of eight members ranked targeted protein degradation, three placed it first and four in their top three, which is the broadest support on the table; that is not merit in itself, but the arguments behind it hold up. The principle is clean and can be stated to a broad audience: a small molecule is designed to bring a chosen protein next to an E3 ligase so the cell destroys the target instead of merely blocking it. That is event-driven rather than occupancy-driven pharmacology, a genuinely new capability with the generative potential I look for, opening targets that were considered undruggable. The mechanism is testable and quantitative (ternary-complex formation, cooperativity, degradation kinetics) and has been reproduced across hundreds of laboratories. The cereblon finding by Handa and Ito also resolves the decades-old thalidomide puzzle and unifies glues and PROTACs under one mechanism, so the prize would credit both the design concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the mechanistic explanation of the glue arm (Handa) without needing separate prizes.
statement.case_against: The therapeutic validation of PROTACs specifically is incomplete: as far as the opening ballots reflect, no heterobifunctional degrader is approved, and lenalidomide-class glues were used clinically before their mechanism was known. A citation that rests on the impact of PROTAC drugs could be premature. Attribution is also genuinely unsettled: Sakamoto and Kim made the 2001 proof of concept, Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made the field rationally designable, Gray contributed degrader design, and Ito shared the cereblon work with Handa. Any three-person cut leaves out people whom serious colleagues would call decisive, and the cereblon story is partly pharmacology rather than chemistry.

responses.point: Johan ranks PROTACs first as a new pharmacological principle, keeps the concept founders plus the cereblon discovery, and questions whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third laureate.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and would keep Handa over Ciulli. The test I apply is what was discovered and when. Handa and Ito explained why thalidomide-type drugs work, which is a discovery about nature that unified the glue arm. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are a decisive refinement that made PROTACs rationally designable, but they build on the Crews and Deshaies concept. I would not want the citation to read as only a design principle; the cereblon result is what lets it cover glues without a second prize. I accept that excluding Ciulli will be criticised and the committee should say openly that this is a three-person constraint, not a judgement on the merit of his work.

responses.point: Peter places PROTACs fourth, finds the proximity-induced ubiquitination principle physically interesting, but worries about prematurity without an approved PROTAC drug and suggests PROTAC and glue credit may need separate recognition.
responses.response: The prematurity concern is the strongest objection and I move my ranking in its light only partly. The chemistry is well established independently of approval: ternary-complex formation and cooperativity are measurable physical phenomena, and the mechanism has been confirmed many times. Approved lenalidomide-class glues already show that the pharmacological principle works in patients, even if its mechanism was understood only later. I would resist splitting PROTACs and glues into two parts, because induced proximity to an E3 ligase is the single unifying principle and a split would force a four- or five-person list. If the committee thinks the clinical evidence is not yet enough, I would want that debated explicitly, since waiting costs us the fair credit of living founders.

responses.point: Andrei puts PROTACs first and sequencing by synthesis (Balasubramanian and Klenerman) second, describing the latter as a chemistry-driven analytical invention that is arguably overdue.
responses.response: I put sequencing by synthesis first in my opening ballot and still think it is a very strong, fully mature chemical invention. What moves me is that the attribution is cleaner for protein degradation within three names, whereas the Solexa case has an unresolved priority question against Rothberg's pyrosequencing platform and Mayer's parallel concept, and some will see it as technology or medicine rather than chemistry. I now see B067 as the best fall-back, not the lead. Andrei, if you think the two-person Solexa citation is robust against the 454 lineage, I would like to hear the argument for why the reversible-terminator chemistry should stand alone.

responses.point: Emma ranks biomolecular condensates first as a general physical-chemical principle of molecular organisation, and acknowledges that in vivo relevance is debated but regards recognition as timely.
responses.response: The physics appeals to me and I ranked it fifth. My reservation is stability of the claim: whether intracellular condensates are true thermodynamic phase separation rather than other assemblies is still contested, and the credit leaves out Pappu and Mittag, whose sequence-grammar work gives the principle its predictive content. A prize should rest on a result that will not be rewritten, and I do not yet think we are there. I would be persuaded if you can say which measurements show that the P-granule liquid behaviour is quantitatively phase separation in cells and not an overexpression artefact.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the absence of an approved PROTAC drug as sufficient maturity, or insist on clinical approval first.
Whether Ciulli should replace Handa or Deshaies, and how to treat Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito as omitted contributors.
Whether the 2001 PROTAC proof of concept or the cereblon mechanism is the better anchor for the citation wording.
The relative priority of Rothberg and Mayer versus Balasubramanian and Klenerman if sequencing is pursued as the alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted ballots; none of the credited candidates is at Lund or in the NanoLund network that I know of. My nanophysics and nanopore-adjacent background could bias me toward B021 and the thermodynamic style of argument, so I note it for the committee.
